Cat eyes glow. Yours don't.
Green or gold?
Cat eyes glow. Yours don't.
Shine a light at a cat
in the dark,
and its eyes light up.
Yours don't.
Cat eyes don't make
light.
They bounce yours back.
Behind the retina sits
a mirror layer,
the tapetum lucidum.
Light that slips past
the retina hits it,
and goes back through
for a second chance.
Some of it escapes,
straight back toward
your light.
That's the glow.
So a cat sees with about
a sixth of the light you
need.
The price:
a slightly blurrier picture.
